html:
A book by the historian Procopius that attacks the emperor Justinian, the empress Theodora, the general Belisarius and his wife Antonina. It was probably written around 550 and kept hidden; it is not known to have circulated in the author's lifetime.

Procopius presents it as the truth he could not put in his official History of the Wars for fear of the rulers. In it Justinian is a greedy tyrant, even a demon in human form, who ruined the empire with taxes, wars and new laws. Theodora's early life is described with crude sexual scandal. Belisarius is shown as a fool ruled by his wife.

Historians treat it with care: it is full of spite and exaggeration, yet it gives names and details found nowhere else. It was known in Byzantium as the Anecdota, "unpublished things". A copy was found in the Vatican Library and printed in 1623.
